basic_info.name: Gemma 4 (edge variants E2B, E4B, 12B Unified; full family E2B/E4B/12B/26B A4B/31B)
basic_info.description: Gemma 4 is Google DeepMind's open-weights multimodal model family launched 2026-03-31 and announced 2026-04-02, and the first Gemma generation released under the OSI-approved Apache-2.0 license with no usage thresholds or field-of-use restrictions - a decisive change from the custom Gemma licence of Gemma 1-3. It ships in five sizes: two edge models using Per-Layer Embeddings (E2B, 2.3B effective; E4B, 4.5B effective), an encoder-free 12B Unified model, a 26B A4B Mixture-of-Experts model and a 31B dense model, all handling text plus image and audio (31B text+image), with 128K context on E4B/E2B and 256K on the larger sizes, native function calling/JSON and 140+ languages. The single most load-bearing fact for MediKiosk is that Google publishes measured CPU and edge tables rather than marketing claims: Gemma-4-E4B is a 3.65GB model that runs on CPU at 18 decode tokens/s on an x86 Linux host with ~3.1GB peak memory and at 3 tokens/s on a Raspberry Pi 5 with ~3.1GB peak memory - i.e. the top of the edge tier is genuinely on the boundary of MediKiosk's ~4GB CPU/iGPU budget, while E2B sits comfortably inside it. Multiple India-focused Gemma 4 projects (Sakhi for ASHA workers, SAHELI, FieldMedic, ASHA-Saathi, SAHAYAK-TB, VoiceDoc AI) already run offline Hindi/Indic structured extraction and health-form filling at this size, which is exactly the engine role Module C needs.
basic_info.organization: Google DeepMind (released with the Google Open Source and Google AI Edge teams)
basic_info.country: United States (global open-weights distribution; significant India hackathon and public-health adoption)
basic_info.status: production - open-weights family released and actively maintained; Gemma 4 model card last updated 2026-07-30; 12B Unified added 2026-06-03; technical report published 2026-07-02

technical_features.what_it_does: Gemma 4 is a general-purpose multimodal generative model family for text generation, summarization, reasoning, coding and agentic/tool use, explicitly documented for question answering, summarization and reasoning tasks, and deployable on device. For Module C's engine lane it supplies three things: (1) a small, permissively licensed, offline-capable text model (E2B/E4B) that fits kiosk-class hardware; (2) reliable structured output - native function calling and JSON mode - which is what a HistoryBundle-to-summary pipeline needs for machine-checkable section emission rather than free prose; and (3) strong multilingual coverage including Hindi (140+ languages, MMMLU 76.6 for E4B and 67.4 for E2B). Indian community builds have already demonstrated the exact pattern at this size: Sakhi runs E2B on-device and E4B on a workstation to convert Hindi home-visit speech into structured government health forms with function calling and danger-sign flagging; SAHELI fine-tunes E4B for clinical decision support with native FHIR R4 function calling. It is not a clinical model - there is no medical grounding or clinical safety tuning in the base weights - so it is a component of Module C, not the clinical contract.
technical_features.architecture: Decoder-only transformer family with dense and Mixture-of-Experts variants. E2B and E4B use Per-Layer Embeddings (PLE) - each decoder layer has its own small embedding per token, so the embedding tables are large but only used for quick lookups, giving a low effective parameter count (2.3B and 4.5B effective versus 5.1B and 8B including embeddings). E2B has 35 layers, E4B 42, 12B 48, 31B 60; sliding window 512-1024 tokens; 262K vocabulary. Multimodal support uses a frozen ~150M vision encoder and ~300M audio encoder on E2B/E4B; the 12B Unified model removes encoders entirely and projects raw 48x48x3 image patches and 40ms audio chunks into the LLM embedding space via lightweight linear layers (~35M-parameter vision matmul), reducing multimodal latency and memory fragmentation. A built-in thinking mode generates reasoning traces before answering, and Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) draft models accelerate decoding.
technical_features.inputs: Text, images (variable aspect ratio; document/PDF parsing, OCR including multilingual, handwriting recognition, chart comprehension, screen/UI understanding, object detection and pointing) and audio (speech understanding/ASR and speech-to-translated-text) on E2B, E4B and 12B; the 31B model is text+image only. Images are handled at variable resolution; the family supports long documents within its context window. No structured clinical inputs (no FHIR, no slots) are defined natively - those must be serialized into the prompt by the calling application.
technical_features.outputs: Generated text, optionally interleaved with a reasoning trace when thinking mode is enabled, plus native tool/function calls and JSON. There is no native FHIR, Composition, Bundle or NRCeS OPConsultRecord output; any such emission is written by the calling application (as SAHELI does with FHIR tool functions). Output length is large enough for note generation; on-device mobile quantizations are the limiting factor, not output size.
technical_features.standards_compliance: No clinical or interoperability standard is claimed for the base models - Gemma 4 is not FHIR, HL7 IPS, SNOMED CT, LOINC or NRCeS conformant, and no conformance is validated. What it does provide is the general mechanism (native function calling/JSON) with which an application can emit standards-conformant structures; community fine-tunes have wrapped it into FHIR R4 function calling (SAHELI) but that is third-party, not model-level conformance. For Module C, Gemma 4 would be the NLU/summarization layer behind a deterministic, validator-checked NRCeS renderer. [Any model-level ABDM/FHIR conformance: not applicable - uncertain that any is intended]
technical_features.offline_capability: Strong and first-class. Gemma 4 runs fully offline on CPU/GPU/NPU through Google AI Edge's LiteRT-LM (E2B and E4B supported today, with larger sizes coming), through llama.cpp/LM Studio/Ollama GGUF builds (day-one support), and on Android via the built-in AICore system model; WebGPU/browser execution is also offered. Edge variants are explicitly pitched for 'completely offline with near-zero latency' operation on phones, Raspberry Pi and Jetson-class devices. Licensing is offline-friendly (Apache 2.0, no telemetry requirement), but the model itself ships no storage, encryption, sync or store-and-forward layer - those remain the application's responsibility. [Store-and-forward behaviour: not applicable to the model - application concern]
technical_features.languages_supported: 140+ languages with multilingual support, including Hindi. Model-card multilingual benchmark MMMLU: 88.4 (31B), 86.3 (26B A4B), 83.4 (12B), 76.6 (E4B), 67.4 (E2B). E2B/E4B/12B also support audio ASR and speech-to-translated-text across multiple languages. India-specific evidence is unusually direct: Sakhi implements Hindi number/word normalization and Hindi voice-to-form extraction on E2B/E4B, ASHA-Saathi targets Hindi/Marathi, and FieldMedic covers English, Hindi, Bengali, Tamil and Marathi with structured JSON output at 100% valid-JSON rate. Whether Hindi clinical summarization quality (as opposed to structured extraction) is adequate still needs the team's own evaluation.
technical_features.deployment_model: Deployment spans phone to workstation. Mobile: E2B/E4B on Android and iOS via LiteRT-LM and Android AICore; desktop/web: Windows, Linux, macOS (Metal) and WebGPU; IoT/robotics: Raspberry Pi 5 and Qualcomm Dragonwing IQ8/Arduino VENTUNO Q; workstation: 26B A4B and 31B for consumer GPUs. Measured LiteRT-LM CPU numbers for E4B: Linux ARM 82 prefill / 18 decode tok/s with 12.6s TTFT and 3139MB peak; Raspberry Pi 5 16GB 51 prefill / 3 decode with 20.5s TTFT and 3069MB peak; macOS M4 Max 277/27; Windows Intel LunarLake 173/17 with 6.0s TTFT. Higher-RAM Android phones reach 195 prefill / 18 decode with 3283MB peak. The model file is 3.65GB; cloud hosting is also available (Vertex AI, Google Cloud) but is not required. Edge deployment is realistic at kiosk scale but tight at the top: E4B's ~3.1GB measured peak on Linux ARM/Raspberry Pi CPU fits a ~4GB budget with little headroom for the application, ASR and storage, while E2B's ~1-3GB is comfortable; BF16 E4B is 17.9GB and SFP8 8.9GB, so only 4-bit or mobile quantizations are viable on MediKiosk hardware.

performance_metrics.accuracy_or_quality_metrics: Vendor model-card benchmarks: E4B MMLU Pro 69.4, GPQA Diamond 58.6, MMMLU 76.6, AIME 2026 no-tools 42.5, LiveCodeBench v6 52.0, Codeforces ELO 940, Tau2 42.2, BigBench Extra Hard 33.1; E2B MMLU Pro 60.0, GPQA Diamond 43.4, MMMLU 67.4. For scale, 31B reaches MMLU Pro 85.2, GPQA Diamond 84.3 and Arena Elo 1452. Independent controlled benchmark (arXiv 2604.07035, 8,400 model-dataset-prompt evaluations): Gemma-4-E4B with few-shot chain-of-thought achieved the best weighted multi-task accuracy in the study at 0.675 (ARC-Challenge 0.900, TruthfulQA 0.800) with mean 14.9GB VRAM; Gemma-4-26B-A4B was close at 0.663 but at 48.1GB; Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-30B-A3B and Phi-4-mini-reasoning lagged notably in aggregate accuracy (Qwen3-30B-A3B best weighted accuracy 0.226). No vendor or third-party benchmark exists for clinical summarization, ROUGE/BERTScore on clinical notes, or Hindi clinical note quality - the India evidence is structured-extraction accuracy (100% valid JSON, >95% schema conformance, 85% severity correctness for FieldMedic E2B; 90% tier accuracy for SAHAYAK-TB).
performance_metrics.latency: Measured LiteRT-LM CPU throughput for Gemma-4-E4B: Linux ARM 82 prefill / 18 decode tok/s, TTFT 12.6s, peak 3139MB; Raspberry Pi 5 16GB 51 prefill / 3 decode tok/s, TTFT 20.5s, peak 3069MB; macOS M4 Max 277 prefill / 27 decode tok/s, TTFT 3.7s; Windows Intel LunarLake 173 prefill / 17 decode tok/s, TTFT 6.0s, peak 9372MB; Android S26 Ultra CPU 195 prefill / 18 decode tok/s, TTFT 5.3s, peak 3283MB; iOS iPhone 17 Pro CPU 159/10, TTFT 6.5s. GPU numbers are 22-101 decode tok/s depending on device. Realistic applied latencies from India projects: Sakhi reports ~15-25s end-to-end voice-to-form on an RTX 5070 Ti/T4 workstation, and ~5 minutes for the fully on-device E2B text-to-form pipeline on a Snapdragon 8+ Gen 1 phone; SAHAYAK-TB reports 24-88s CPU-only per case on E2B Q4_K_M. No time-to-summary figure exists for E4B on a ~4GB kiosk CPU, which is the configuration MediKiosk would use.
performance_metrics.resource_requirements: Model sizes and precisions (Google model overview): E2B BF16 11.4GB / SFP8 5.7GB / Q4_0 2.9GB / mobile 1.1GB / mobile text-only 0.84GB; E4B BF16 17.9GB / SFP8 8.9GB / Q4_0 4.5GB / mobile 2.5GB / mobile text-only 2.2GB; 12B Q4_0 6.7GB; 26B A4B Q4_0 14.4GB; 31B Q4_0 17.5GB. LiteRT-LM E4B model file 3.65GB with measured CPU peak memory of ~3.1GB (Linux ARM, Raspberry Pi 5) to ~3.3GB (high-end Android). Practical guidance from the community: E4B recommended as the safest local starting point for laptop-class setups at about 5GB in Q4, running on 8GB unified memory; E2B INT4 mobile package ~4.4GB download / ~6.3GB extracted when the multimodal audio+vision encoders are included. Implication for MediKiosk: E2B (Q4/mobile 0.84-2.9GB) fits a ~4GB kiosk; E4B at Q4 (4.5GB weights, ~3.1-5GB runtime) is at or just over the boundary and needs headroom budgeting; 12B and above are out of scope.
performance_metrics.scale_metrics: Family-level: Google reported over 400 million Gemma downloads and more than 100,000 community variants at the Gemma 4 launch, and a Gemma 4 Good Hackathon produced India-focused health submissions (Sakhi, VoiceDoc AI, FieldMedic, ASHA-Saathi, SAHAYAK-TB). Note that these are family-level and ecosystem-level figures, not Gemma 4 edge adoption counts. No deployment counts, patient/record volumes or enterprise adoption numbers are published for the edge variants specifically. Ollama/LM Studio/local-runtime pull counts for Gemma 4 E2B/E4B are not surfaced here. [Edge-variant adoption: uncertain - family-level only]
performance_metrics.evaluation_protocol: Two evidence layers. (1) Vendor: the Gemma 4 model card and the Gemma 4 Technical Report (arXiv 2607.02770) report reproducible benchmark scores across reasoning, coding, STEM, multimodal and long-context tasks, plus human-rated Arena Elo; these are vendor-run evaluations. (2) Independent: the controlled arXiv 2604.07035 benchmark compares Gemma-4-E2B/E4B/26B-A4B against Phi-4 and Qwen3 models across ARC-Challenge, GSM8K, Math Level 1-3 and TruthfulQA under zero-shot, CoT and few-shot CoT prompting, with 8,400 evaluations and 252 paired McNemar-style comparisons (181 significant at p<0.05), releasing a reproducible pipeline. Neither layer evaluates clinical summarization, so the Module C team must run its own harness (the established clinical protocol is ROUGE/BERTScore/BLEURT plus concept recall and inference-aware human/LLM judging).

milestone_significance.relevance_to_module_c: Gemma 4 is the strongest permissively licensed, small, offline-capable engine option the Module C research sweep has found, and it directly addresses the three constraints that eliminate most competitors. (1) Offline CPU footprint: Google's own measured tables put E4B at ~3.1GB peak CPU memory and E2B comfortably lower, which is the only published evidence of a 2026 frontier-family model running inside kiosk-class memory. (2) Licensing: Apache-2.0 with no MAU thresholds or field-of-use carve-outs removes the legal review friction that Gemma 1-3 and MedGemma carry, which matters for a Ministry of Ayush/AIIA product. (3) Structured emission: native function calling and JSON mode give Module C a machine-checkable path from HistoryBundle fields to rendered summary sections, and multiple India projects already use it for exactly that. It also supplies the multilingual lane (Hindi/Indic) that MedGemma does not. The caveat is that Gemma 4 is general-purpose with no clinical safety tuning, so it validates the engine choice but does not supply the clinical contract, the provenance model or the attestation gate.
milestone_significance.what_to_adopt_or_reject: Adopt: (1) Gemma 4 E2B and/or E4B with llama.cpp/Ollama or LiteRT-LM as the local summarization/NLU engine lane, with E2B as the default inside the ~4GB budget and E4B reserved for a room-server or a headroom-verified kiosk build; (2) native function calling/JSON mode as the mechanism for emitting structured sections, behind a deterministic NRCeS renderer - not as a replacement for it; (3) the multilingual lane (Hindi/Devanagari) for the read-back and bilingual summary; (4) the Indian community patterns as design references - Sakhi's Hindi number normalization for compound clinical values ('110/70', decimals, weights) and its record-now/sync-later offline pattern, SAHELI's FHIR function-call schema, and FieldMedic's explicit no-diagnosis schema design (no 'diagnosis' field; always-escalate on red). Reject: (1) any 12B or larger variant on the kiosk; (2) relying on base Gemma 4 clinical accuracy - the base models are not medically tuned and the team must run its own evaluation harness (ROUGE/BERTScore/concept recall plus a clinician or inference-aware judge) before gating narrative generation; (3) the assumption that native JSON equals FHIR conformance - validation against the NRCeS IG is still required downstream.
milestone_significance.limitations_and_risks: Clinical: no medical fine-tuning or clinical safety evaluation in the base weights, so hallucination and omission risk is real (the India fine-tunes all add explicit refusal/no-diagnosis schemas, and ASHA-Saathi's protocol-accuracy regression shows how fine-tuning for safety can trade off task accuracy); Gemma 4's training-data cutoff is January 2025, so it does not know 2025-2026 medications or protocols. Hardware: E4B at 4-bit is 4.5GB of weights with measured runtime peaks of ~3.1-5GB, which is at or above the ~4GB kiosk budget once ASR, storage and the application are added - the honest position is that E2B fits and E4B is borderline. Latency: on-device decode rates are 3-27 tokens/s on CPU depending on device, and applied India pipelines report ~5 minutes on-device or 15-88s with a workstation; interactive summarization on the kiosk CPU is therefore a batch-style operation, and no kiosk-class time-to-summary figure has been measured. On-device structured output degrades at the smallest tier: E2B INT4 does not reliably emit OpenAI-style tool calls and can echo JSON-schema metadata, requiring a null-filled template workaround. Licensing/quality: Apache-2.0 is clean, but Google's benchmarks are vendor-run and there is no independent clinical-summarization or Hindi-clinical evidence. Ecosystem: 12B and larger require encoders/GPU-class memory, and several third-party 'Gemma 4' comparisons online mix fabricated throughput figures with real ones, so numbers must be checked against the official tables.
milestone_significance.differentiator_vs_medikiosk: Gemma 4 supplies the engine but not the differentiators, which is exactly the right split for MediKiosk. It is a general open-weights model: it has no history elicitation, no HistoryBundle contract, no per-field provenance/confidence, no NRCeS OPConsultRecord emission, no ABDM consent handling and no physician-attestation gate - all of which remain MediKiosk's defensible surface. Because it is Apache-2.0 and runs offline on CPU, adopting it strengthens the offline, India-data-residency and no-cloud-vendor differentiators rather than eroding them (unlike the cloud-backed competitor stack). Versus Qwen3 specifically: Gemma 4 is a generation newer (April 2026 vs Qwen3's April 2025), is natively multimodal while Qwen3 small is text-only, and in the one independent controlled benchmark Gemma-4-E4B outperformed both Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-30B-A3B in weighted accuracy at moderate memory. Qwen3 still has genuine advantages - a smaller 1.7B option at ~2.4GB RAM with a very small footprint and Apache-2.0 licensing, older/more mature tooling, and larger MoE siblings - so the honest conclusion is that Qwen3 1.7B/4B and Gemma 4 E2B/E4B are the two viable permissive offline lanes, with Gemma 4 favoured on recency, multimodal support, multilingual breadth and measured edge data, and Qwen3 favoured if the absolute minimum memory footprint dominates. Gemma 4 does erode one thing: its availability makes 'we run a local model' a commodity claim, so MediKiosk's differentiation must rest on the clinical contract, provenance, validation and attestation rather than on the engine itself.

business_info.license: Apache License 2.0 (OSI-approved) for all Gemma 4 models and weights - the first Gemma generation released under Apache 2.0, explicitly granting commercial use, modification, redistribution and derivative works with no monthly-active-user thresholds and no field-of-use restrictions. The model card confirms 'Gemma 4 is licensed under the Apache-2.0 license.' This is a deliberate change from the custom Gemma licence (with Prohibited Use Policy) of Gemma 1-3, which is why the change is often described as removing procurement and legal-review friction.
business_info.pricing: Model weights are free of charge to download and self-host (Hugging Face, Kaggle, Vertex AI). Paid cost appears only for cloud hosting: Vertex AI dedicated endpoints and Google Cloud serving. No per-seat or per-device fee, no usage caps. Local inference via Ollama/llama.cpp/LiteRT-LM has no licence cost.
business_info.funding: Google-internal research and product effort (Google DeepMind, Google AI Edge, Google Open Source); no external funding round is relevant to an open-weights release.
business_info.commercial_status: Free open-weights release from Google with unrestricted commercial use; not a commercial product or paid service. It is a developer model/platform play rather than a revenue-bearing product.

competition_ecosystem.competitors: Qwen3 small dense models (1.7B / 4B, Apache-2.0, ~2.5-3.3GB at Q4-Q8, Hindi-capable, text-only) are the closest direct alternative for the offline engine lane, with Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-30B-A3B as larger siblings; newer Qwen 3.5/3.6/3.8 generations (some Apache-2.0, one custom-licensed) now exist but at larger sizes. Other alternatives: Llama 3.x/4 small, Phi-4-mini(-reasoning), Ministral/Mistral small, and Gemma 3 (previous generation). In the clinical-engine space the overlaps are CureNet (which runs Gemma 4 E4B + 31B), MedGemma (gated, non-permissive) and clinical fine-tunes of Gemma 4 itself (SAHELI, ASHA-Saathi, FieldMedic, SAHAYAK-TB).
competition_ecosystem.integrations: Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio and other GGUF runtimes (day-one support); Google AI Edge LiteRT-LM (E2B/E4B today); Android AICore system model; WebGPU browser execution; Hugging Face and Kaggle distribution; Vertex AI/Google Cloud hosting; the Cactus SDK for on-device Android (used by Sakhi); Unsloth/TRL and PEFT/QLoRA for fine-tuning; and community wrappers such as SAHELI's FHIR R4 tool functions. No native EHR/HIS or ABDM HIP/HIU integration exists - that is application work.
competition_ecosystem.ecosystem_notes: Two ecosystem signals matter for MediKiosk. First, the Apache-2.0 relicense plus a mature GGUF/LiteRT toolchain has removed the last procurement objection to Gemma on regulated/offline devices, which is precisely why the India health-hackathon ecosystem standardised on Gemma 4 E2B/E4B for offline Hindi structured extraction - the same pattern Module C needs, already prototyped publicly. Second, the competitive bar is rising without the engine being a differentiator: CureNet already runs Gemma 4 E4B/31B locally, so 'runs a local small model' is now table stakes and MediKiosk's defensibility must come from the clinical contract (NRCeS OPConsultRecord), provenance, validation artifacts and physician attestation. The main ecosystem risk is quantitative noise - community 'Gemma 4 vs Qwen3' comparisons mix measured and fabricated figures - so the team should benchmark E2B/E4B on its own kiosk hardware rather than trust third-party tables.

history.release_date: 2026-03-31 (Gemma 4 E2B, E4B, 31B and 26B A4B released; public launch blogs dated 2026-04-02). Gemma 4 12B Unified released 2026-06-03. Gemma 4 Technical Report published 2026-07-02.
history.key_milestones: 2026-03-31 - Gemma 4 released in E2B, E4B, 31B and 26B A4B sizes, the first Gemmaverse generation under Apache 2.0. 2026-04-02 - launch blogs from Google DeepMind, Google AI Edge and Google Open Source; Google reports 400M+ Gemma downloads and 100,000+ variants, and positions Gemma 4 for mobile/desktop/web/IoT deployment (Android AICore, LiteRT-LM, Raspberry Pi 5, Qualcomm Dragonwing IQ8); independent controlled benchmark arXiv 2604.07035 published 2026-04-08. 2026-04-16 - further Gemma release activity (per the releases timeline). 2026-06-03 - Gemma 4 12B Unified (encoder-free multimodal) released, targeting laptops. 2026-07-02 - Gemma 4 Technical Report (arXiv 2607.02770 published Jul 2). 2026-07-30 - Gemma 4 model card last updated (current published specs and benchmark table). In parallel Google ran a Gemma 4 Good Hackathon that produced multiple India-focused offline health builds.
history.recent_changes_last_6_months: The entire Gemma 4 family falls inside the last 6 months relative to 2026-09-16: (1) 2026-03-31/04-02 - Gemma 4 launch under Apache 2.0 with E2B, E4B, 26B A4B and 31B, the headline licence change away from the custom Gemma terms; (2) 2026-04-08 - independent accuracy-efficiency benchmark naming Gemma-4-E4B the best overall operating point among Gemma/Phi/Qwen3 models tested; (3) 2026-04-16 - additional release-line activity; (4) 2026-06-03 - Gemma 4 12B Unified (encoder-free, laptop-class); (5) 2026-07-02 - Gemma 4 Technical Report published; (6) 2026-07-30 - model card refreshed with the current precision/quantization and benchmark tables; and (7) a growing set of India-focused Gemma 4 E2B/E4B health fine-tunes and hackathon projects published through mid-2026. No newer Gemma 4 size or a dedicated clinical variant appeared in the window. [Any unindexed Gemma 4 release between 2026-07-30 and 2026-09-16: uncertain - none found]

market_positioning.target_users: Developers, researchers, startups and enterprises building on-device or self-hosted AI - mobile/edge app developers, robotics and IoT builders, and teams with data-sovereignty or offline requirements. In practice the India health ecosystem has adopted the edge variants for frontline health worker tools.
market_positioning.market_segment: Open-weight foundation models / on-device AI engines - the model layer beneath summarization, agents, structured extraction and multimodal apps. It sits underneath, not inside, the intake or FHIR-tooling segments.
market_positioning.positioning_statement: Google positions Gemma 4 as 'our most intelligent open models to date... purpose-built for advanced reasoning and agentic workflows' delivering 'frontier-level performance at each size', with the edge story as 'redefine what is possible on your own hardware... agents and autonomous AI use cases running directly on-device... offline code generation... support for over 140 languages', and the licence as the key enabler: 'released under a commercially permissive Apache 2.0 license... complete developer flexibility and digital sovereignty; granting you complete control over your data, infrastructure, and models.'
